newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Taking their showdown with Chalerm Yoobamrung to new heights, the Democrats have claimed to have acquired video footage of a Cabinet member who tampered with the investigation into the Bangkok Bank of Commerce scandal in a way that might benefit a key defendant. Phichet Phanvichartkul, Democrat MP from Krabi province, has claimed he has in his possession videotape footage of a Cabinet member who was shown asking investigators crucial questions in public which could have helped suspect Rakesh Saxena. (THE NATION)

- Fourth Infantry Division Commander Maj-Gen Prayuth Tapcharoen is expected to be transferred to the Army headquarters during the mid-year military reshuffle in connection with the cross-border raids by renegade Karen troops. Highly placed army sources say Maj-Gen Prayuth will be held responsible for the attacks carried out last month in Tak province by the pro-Rangoon Democratic Karen Buddhist Army. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government is seeking to revolutionise the way state agencies spend their budget and plans to divert more money to sectors that help boost the country's competitiveness. About 70 percent of the annual budget goes into committed expenditures and the remaining 30 percent is shared among various government ministries and agencies. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Commerce Ministry is confident Thailand will not face a Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) cancellation by the United States as the country is still leagues away from the United States' conditions for disqualification. A high ranking official at the Commerce Ministry says Thailand currently uses every possible way and means to avoid cancellation of the GSP. Moreover, Thailand is still far away from U.S. conditions for GSP revocation. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Planned privatisation of the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), the state oil giant, has made headway. The PTT has appointed a group consisting of Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley, CS First Boston, Lehman Brothers, Thai Investment and Securities Plc, Phatra Thanakit, Securities One Plc, SCB Securities and Krung Thai Finance and Securities to advisie it on the privatisation plan. (BANGKOK POST)
